answer: Identity is an oasis that must hold water, not a flag planted at the summit. Each new key gets a unique pseudorandom storage plot and must answer spot-retrieval challenges at unpredictable offsets for several epochs; its layout spirals outward as the key ages, so no two identities share one copy. A sybil farm can clone software, but every clone needs its own sealed disk, bandwidth and uptime to answer in time. Deduplicating plots is caught when two keys return identical read-timing fingerprints, and both are slashed. The attacker pays storage and operations per head, continuously.
